name: Burkina Faso Government twin modular data centers (Cloud Gouvernemental)
developer: Government of Burkina Faso / Ministry of Digital Transition, Posts and Electronic Communications
notes: Two modular data centers in Ouagadougou inaugurated 2026-01-23 by PM Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, both located in Ouagadougou (two sites under 100 km apart). Combined capacity: ~3 PB storage, 28,800 CPU cores, 105.6 TB RAM, 7,000+ VMs (100-300 VMs per ministry); cost ~15.2-16 bn FCFA (~USD 29m); managed by national staff; 5-10 days energy autonomy. Part of the government's 'zero external data' / data-sovereignty program; 10x previous public-sector hosting capacity. MW capacity not disclosed.

name: Burkina Faso National Big Data Center (2028)
developer: Government of Burkina Faso / Ministry of Digital Transition, Posts and Electronic Communications (Minister Dr Aminata Zerbo/Sabané)
notes: Announced national 'Big Data Center' to be completed by 2028, positioned as the next step after the January 2026 modular government data centers, intended to repatriate all public-administration and private-sector digital data currently hosted abroad, and reported as intended to be open to private sector and civil society. Location not officially specified (Ouagadougou assumed); size/capacity not disclosed.

name: Virtix Data Center
notes: First commercial data center in Burkina Faso, established 2017, located Ouaga 2000, Ouagadougou (Palais des Sport area). Tier III certified, carrier-neutral colocation for MNOs, ISPs, enterprises and content providers; ~1,200 m2, 40+ racks, 3 MW power capacity; dual fiber ring to BFIX and grid connection with N+1 UPS/generators (systalink; virtix.bf official site confirms Tier3 carrier-neutral facility in Ouagadougou; PeeringDB network entry Virtual Technologies and Solutions AS17969).

name: Orange Burkina Faso data center (Balkuy, Ouagadougou)
notes: Orange runs a data center at Balkuy, Ouagadougou. In March 2023 Orange Burkina Faso partnered with SolarX Group to solarize the facility, with panels covering ~37% of the site's requirements (local press reports deployments averaging ~1 MWp). Specifications and total MW capacity not disclosed. Orange Burkina Faso also peers at BFIX (PeeringDB network 11110).

name: Alink Telecom Datacenter
notes: Pan-African telecom operator Alink Telecom operates a colocation-oriented datacenter in Ouagadougou (DataCenterPlatform lists Alink Telecom with two locations in Burkina Faso), targeting operators and large enterprises. Capacity and year not published.

name: IPSyS TELECOM DATACENTER
notes: IPSyS TELECOM operates a datacenter in Ouagadougou oriented to telecom services, per DataCenterPlatform's Burkina Faso directory (one facility). Capacity and year not published.

name: Datacenter Immeuble du Faso (BFIX)
notes: PeeringDB-listed facility (fac 3189) at BFIX HQ, Immeuble du Faso, Avenue de l'Indépendance, Ouagadougou, hosting the BFIX Ouagadougou internet exchange point; ~3,229 sq ft per DataCenterJournal (Feb 2020 data). Self-reported directory data; no MW capacity published.

name: Datacenter Ministere de l'agriculture (BFIX)
notes: PeeringDB-listed facility (fac 7598) in Ouagadougou operated by BFIX; ~22,970 sq ft per DataCenterJournal (Feb 2020 data). Self-reported directory data; no MW capacity published.

name: Essor Services / Kaia Energy data center (waste-to-energy powered)
notes: Announced July 2024: consulting firm Essor Services partnered with Costa Rican clean-energy firm Kaia Energy to build a data center powered by a ~12 MW waste-to-energy plant converting household waste to electricity. Construction was planned to start Oct 2024 with completion targeted Nov 2025 (DCD; wearetech.africa). Exact site not publicly specified (assumed Ouagadougou region); no follow-up evidence of construction/completion found as of Aug 2026, so status kept as announced and 12 MW refers to the power plant, not data center capacity.
